notes: The Acura ZDX was offered only for model year 2024; Acura ended ZDX production in September 2025 with no 2025 or 2026 model year, discontinuing the nameplate. Built on GM's Ultium platform, shared with the Honda Prologue. USB port count reflects the two rear USB-C ports confirmed in Acura's spec sheet; front-row port count was not separately itemized.

Type S adds Brembo brakes, adaptive/air suspension, 22-inch wheels, Hands Free Cruise, and a head-up display. 0-60 time is an approximate figure ("just under 5 seconds" per reviewers); Acura did not publish an exact number. Single-motor RWD entry trim (formerly '40', renamed '45 e-tron' for 2025 with a larger 82 kWh pack). No frunk on Q4 e-tron; deep rear underfloor well instead. Heat pump is not standard on this trim, only available on 55 e-tron quattro via the Cold Weather Package.

No SQ4 e-tron performance model currently exists; this dual-motor 55 e-tron quattro is the top powertrain available for Q4 e-tron. Heat pump available via optional Cold Weather Package (not standard).

First Audi EV on the PPE platform, shared with Porsche Macan Electric. Battery listed by sources as a '100 kWh' pack; some outlets cite ~94.9 kWh usable net -- used the figure as directly reported. No-cost Ultra package adds heated steering wheel/heated rear seats on some configurations. 456 hp figure is the launch-control peak (422 hp continuous).

Audi's original e-tron (MLB EV) platform SUV, being phased out; still native CCS1, with an Audi NACS DC adapter available as an accessory. Small frunk exists but no published cubic-foot figure found. Max DC charge rate and AC onboard charger kW not confirmed from a reliable source this session, left null rather than guessed.

Performance flagship of the Q6 e-tron line; 509 hp is the launch-control peak (483 hp / 631 lb-ft standard). Standard sport-tuned adaptive air suspension. Cargo figures assumed identical to Q6 e-tron (shared body shell); tow rating not separately confirmed for SQ6.

notes: Redesigned 2025 e-tron GT is renamed 'S e-tron GT' in the US; 'Premium Plus' is the entry trim (no plain 'Premium' trim found for this generation). 670 hp is the boost/launch-control peak (583 hp standard). 912 hp / 2.4s 0-60 figures are with launch control engaged (RS e-tron GT performance is the only RS trim for 2025). Cargo figures assumed identical to S e-tron GT (shared body); not separately confirmed.

Base RWD trim of BMW's 4 Series Gran Coupe-based liftback sedan. For 2026 BMW added silicon-carbide inverters, raising EPA range vs prior model year. Standard driver-assist items (forward collision warning w/ automatic braking, lane departure warning) are part of BMW's standard active-safety suite; full adaptive cruise + lane centering requires the optional Driving Assistant Professional package. Charge port is CCS1 (adapter needed for Tesla Superchargers); no factory tow rating published for i4 in the US. Cargo, USB port count, and some seat-comfort options could not be confirmed from public sources.

For model year 2026 BMW replaced the prior i4 M50 with the more powerful M60 xDrive as the top i4 trim (593 hp, dual motor AWD, 130 mph top speed / 140 mph with optional High Performance Tire Package on 20-inch wheels). Top speed and torque not fully confirmed from public manufacturer pages. Driving Assistant Professional (adaptive cruise, lane centering) is an optional package rather than standard equipment.

As of March 2026 production, BMW switched the entire i5 lineup (including eDrive40) to a native NACS charge port with bundled J1772 and CCS1 adapters; earlier-built 2026 cars shipped with CCS1 and received a software update enabling Supercharger access. Standard active-safety suite (blind spot detection, lane keeping assistant, forward collision mitigation, speed limit assistant) is standard equipment per BMW USA; full adaptive cruise/lane centering requires optional Driving Assistant Professional. Battery usable kWh assumed to match the i4's shared 5th-generation eDrive pack (81.2 kWh usable / 84.3 kWh gross); not separately itemized by BMW for i5 specifically.

The i5 M60 xDrive was the first BMW sold in the US with a native NACS charge port (added for 2026); it ships with adapters for legacy CCS1/J1772 equipment. Torque figures for M60 vary by source (586-605 lb-ft); omitted here for lack of a single authoritative figure. Top speed not confirmed for M60.

Flagship long-wheelbase electric 7 Series sedan; rear seats do not fold, so no expanded cargo figure applies. BMW plans to add a native NACS port to the i7 lineup starting with the 2027 model year - the 2026 xDrive60 tested here still uses CCS1. 0-60 time is a commonly cited BMW figure but was not directly confirmed on a manufacturer spec page during this research pass; top speed and tow rating are not published for the US market.

For 2026 the former 516-hp xDrive50 was replaced by the 536-hp xDrive60 as BMW's mid-tier iX; the requested 'xDrive50' name is no longer offered for MY2026, so this entry reflects the current equivalent trim. The iX has no frunk because its hood does not open. US tow rating of 3,500 lb (factory tow package required) is commonly cited by BMW dealers; European braked tow rating for the same platform is listed higher (2,500 kg / ~5,512 lb) but that figure isn't confirmed for US-spec vehicles, so the more conservative US figure is used. Ground clearance not confirmed to a reliable inch figure from public sources.

Top performance iX trim, replacing the prior M60 as BMW's flagship electric SUV. Torque reaches 811 lb-ft briefly under Launch Control (749 lb-ft sustained). Tow capacity assumed equal to xDrive60's US rating (3,500 lb with factory tow package); not separately published for M70. Ground clearance not confirmed.

First US 'Neue Klasse' platform BMW, officially announced by BMW press release in May 2026 with confirmed on-sale date of September 25, 2026. 800V architecture with 400 kW max DC charging (10-80% in ~21 min) and native NACS port; supports bidirectional (V2L/V2H) charging per BMW's announcement. Base MSRP of $61,500 excludes $1,350 destination/handling. At launch, ventilated front seats and heated rear seats were reported as not yet available (expected to be added later), so those are marked false rather than null. Torque, top speed, ground clearance, tow rating, and exact USB port counts were not disclosed in BMW's initial press materials reviewed.

At time of research this vehicle's EPA rating was not yet indexed as its own listing on fueleconomy.gov; range figure is the manufacturer/EPA-reported 465-mi rating as cited by U.S. News. 800V architecture supports up to 350 kW DC fast charging. Super Cruise standard (incl. auto lane change), treated here as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance, not autonomous self-driving.

Premium Sport adds power-opening front/rear doors, 24-in wheels (up from 22-in standard), and dual power captain's chairs. EPA rating not independently found on fueleconomy.gov at time of research; figure carried over from Luxury trim (same battery/motors). Super Cruise standard, treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance, not autonomous self-driving.

102 kWh is Cadillac's published 'Battery Rated Energy' (total pack); usable capacity is somewhat lower per third-party estimates but no clean official usable figure was found. RWD Lyriq is not tow-rated (towCapacityLbs left null); AWD adds a 3,500 lb tow rating. 0-60 time not confirmed specifically for RWD (a 2023-era Car and Driver test cited 4.6s but that may reflect a different model-year/trim, so left null rather than guess). Super Cruise hands-free driving is available; GM's typical post-trial subscription price (~$25/mo) used, not independently re-verified for MY2025 Lyriq specifically. No frunk on Lyriq. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, $25/mo after trial) is offered on this trim; treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance rather than self-driving, for consistency with the rest of the dataset.

Dual-motor AWD, 515 hp / 450 lb-ft, 22-inch 'After Midnight' finish wheels standard on Sport. 0-60 of 5.1s sourced from a Consumer Reports/Clean Fleet Report test of the same 515hp AWD powertrain (test vehicle was a MY2026 Signature Sport AWD; figure should be very close for MY2025 Sport AWD but wasn't independently tested for MY2025 specifically). Exact Sport 1 AWD MSRP varies across sources ($62k-$65k range seen); $62,590 used as a reasonable estimate off the Luxury AWD price plus the typical Sport premium — treat as approximate rather than a confirmed manufacturer figure. 19.2 kW Level 2 charger listed as it's the AWD-available upgraded onboard charger seen in EPA test configs; base charger may be lower (11.5 kW). Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, $25/mo after trial) is offered on this trim; treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance rather than self-driving, for consistency with the rest of the dataset.

Optiq is AWD-only in the US -- no single-motor FWD trim is offered; every Luxury and Sport trim gets standard dual-motor AWD (front motor primary, rear engages as needed). Apple CarPlay/Android Auto were dropped from US-market Cadillac EVs in favor of Google built-in (still offered in some other markets). Super Cruise hands-free driving comes with a complimentary 3-year trial, then $25/month standalone (or $15/month bundled with OnStar Connected Services). Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, $25/mo after trial) is offered on this trim; treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance rather than self-driving, for consistency with the rest of the dataset.

Mechanically identical to Luxury AWD; Sport trims differ mainly in styling (gloss-black exterior accents/dark badging vs Luxury's Galvano Chrome trim). Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist, $25/mo after trial) is offered on this trim; treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance rather than self-driving, for consistency with the rest of the dataset.
Standard 11.5 kW onboard charger yields 305-mi EPA range. Super Cruise hands-free highway assist is standard but treated here as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance, not autonomous self-driving.

Uses native CCS1 port for 2026 model year with optional NACS Level 2 (AC-only) adapter; DC fast charging remains CCS1. 0-60 time is an approximate figure from press estimates, not an independently verified test. Tow capacity of 1,500 lb requires the optional Trailering Provisions package.

Uses native CCS1 port for 2026 model year; DC fast charging remains CCS1 (optional NACS adapter is AC/Level 2 only). Super Cruise availability on Blazer EV LT/RS not independently confirmed for this trim, so selfDriving.available is set to false pending verification. 0-60 time is an approximate figure from press estimates.

First deliveries began around March 2026, so already broadly on sale. Uses a new 65 kWh LFP (CATL) pack in a cell-to-pack design with native NACS port. GM removed Apple CarPlay/Android Auto in favor of built-in Google-based infotainment for this generation. Super Cruise available as an option (confirmed on RS; may also be optional on LT) is treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance, not autonomous self-driving. Some early reporting cited a $29,990 starting price before the finalized $28,995 LT MSRP.

Super Cruise is treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance, not autonomous self-driving. GM removed Apple CarPlay/Android Auto for this generation.

Uses native CCS1 port for 2026 model year (GM has announced the 2027 Equinox EV switches to native NACS); optional NACS AC adapter exists but DC fast charging remains CCS1. Wireless phone charging is standard only on LT2/RS trims, not base LT1. No Apple CarPlay/Android Auto - Chevy uses Google built-in infotainment instead. Super Cruise is an option on LT2/RS, not available on base LT.

RS AWD MSRP based on 2026 pricing reports (~$44,095-$44,600 depending on source). GM's fueleconomy.gov listing offers two AWD sub-variants (11kW and 19kW onboard charger) with slightly different range (307 vs 288 mi); this entry uses the 11kW/307-mile variant. Super Cruise (hands-free highway driver-assist) is offered on this trim; treated as adaptive-cruise-tier assistance rather than self-driving, for consistency with the rest of the dataset.

Pickup truck: no enclosed rear cargo hold, so cargo.rearCubicFeet/maxCubicFeet are null (not applicable); storage is via a 10.7 cu ft front 'e-trunk' plus bed. 2-door liftback body (hatchback cargo access). 630 hp continuous / up to 670 hp for ~15s via PowerShot mode (627 lb-ft); horsepowerHp field reflects the peak PowerShot rating commonly advertised. Range/MPGe vary by wheel/tire package (216-279 mi across configurations); figures shown are for the highest-range 305/35ZR20 configuration.

2-door liftback body (hatchback cargo access), 496 hp includes factory Direct Connection Stage 1 (404 lb-ft). Range/MPGe vary by wheel/tire package (268-308 mi across configurations); figures shown are for the highest-range 255/45R20 configuration.

Lane Keeping/Adaptive Cruise Control are available options rather than standard on the base RED trim. Adaptive Cruise Control and Active Lane Management System are listed by Stellantis as available (optional) rather than confirmed standard equipment.

Pickup truck: no enclosed rear cargo hold, so cargo.rearCubicFeet/maxCubicFeet are null (not applicable); storage is via the 14.1 cu ft 'Mega Power Frunk' plus the 5.5 ft bed. Charging port listed as NACS reflecting Ford's industry-wide transition to native NACS inlets; not independently re-confirmed on a Ford spec sheet this session. Seat material is Ford's synthetic "ActiveX" leatherette (no genuine leather is offered on any Mach-E trim), so leatherAvailable is false.

DC fast charging is listed at 150 kW to match the same Extended Range pack used on GT, rather than the 115 kW figure that applies to the smaller Standard Range pack (Select RWD) -- some aggregator sites conflate the two. Wireless charging pad lost standard-equipment status for MY2026 and is now bundled only in the optional Technology Package, so wirelessPhoneCharging is false here despite being standard on GT. Heated steering wheel and heated/ventilated front seats plus a 10-speaker Bang & Olufsen system are confirmed standard on Premium (Ford 2026 order guide). Premium is limited to 19-inch wheels only (no 20/21-inch option, unlike Select and GT). Tow capacity and ground clearance could not be confirmed against a reliable MY2026 US-spec primary source -- some sites show older-model-year or EU-spec (kg/liter) figures for these fields, so they are left null rather than guessed. Cupholder and USB port counts left null for the same reason as the other Mach-E entries. Charging port is native CCS1, consistent with the rest of the MY2026 Mach-E lineup.

MY2026 GT is standard AWD with the Extended Range 98.8 kWh pack (88 kWh usable), 480 hp / 600 lb-ft. Edmunds' own test track measured 3.7s 0-60; Ford's own claim (with the optional GT Performance Upgrade, +100 lb-ft to 700 lb-ft) is 3.3s -- used the independently-tested base-GT figure here rather than the marketing number. Charging port is native CCS1 (not NACS) as of MY2026; NACS Supercharger access requires Ford's separate ~$200 adapter accessory. Ventilated seats are notably NOT offered on GT (only on Premium), despite GT being the top trim -- confirmed via multiple owner/dealer sources. Top speed (124 mph / 200 km/h) and tow capacity could not be confirmed against a primary MY2026 Ford source with high confidence; tow capacity is left null rather than guessed. Cupholder/USB port counts also left null for the same reason.
